answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a publicly auditable stake contract before it may post bids or receive work. The contract releases the stake only after a dispute window, and proven fraud transfers it to affected counterparties. Splitting one operator into a raven, a lantern, and a meadow of identities therefore multiplies the capital tied up; the attacker must fund each identity and risks losing those funds, making mass sybils costly rather than merely easy to create.
